digest.component_or_area: LLM model routing and class selection
propositions: Four hand-built sub-calls in review-plan, review, and review-code workflows bypass model-class configuration by passing raw config to RunRequest without declaring a model class, causing them to inherit cfg.model instead of respecting the configured class vocabulary.

The bypass dominates traffic: overlap-judge alone generates 18 of 23 LLM calls in a plan-review workflow, all routing to direct Anthropic instead of configured Bedrock, invisible to operators who cutover using the documented class-config mechanism.

ticket-digest runs on the ticket store write path via enrich_drain.maybe_drain, sending ticket content to direct Anthropic during routine rebar comment/create operations with no gate invocation or verdict to reveal the bypass.

With a class table configured to differ from cfg.model, the measured configuration shows 4 bypass sites resolving to anthropic (raw cfg) while everything else correctly resolves to bedrock (class-bound), but moving cfg.model to bedrock masks the defect rather than fixing it.

A general provenance analysis of RunRequest construction via AST walk must verify that no hand-built sub-call inherits raw config when a class table is configured, and must fail if new bypassing calls are added.
